etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: An unadapted borrowing from German Schadenfreude (“joy in the misfortune of others”), from Schaden (“damage, misfortune”) + Freude (“joy”). The word gained popularity in English in the late 20th c. and likely entered mainstream usage through an episode of The Simpsons (more in citations).
senses: Malicious enjoyment derived from observing someone else's misfortune; counterempathy.
